name: Rhetorical Structure Depth
description: Analyzes the hierarchical depth and complexity of discourse relations. AI relies on flat, sequential logic ('shallow discourse'), whereas human writing builds complex, deeply nested arguments.
algorithm: Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST) Tree Depth Extraction
mechanism: Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST) models text as a hierarchical tree of relational clauses (e.g., Elaboration, Contrast, Cause). Large Language Models generate text left-to-right, calculating the next most probable token based on the immediate context window. Consequently, AI struggles with macro-level architectural planning. When building an argument, AI tends to use 'flat' or 'shallow' discourse structures—creating a string of equally weighted points (List) or simple explanations (Elaboration) attached directly to the root topic. Every paragraph is a standalone silo. Humans, however, naturally construct deep, nested logical hierarchies. A human might nest a Condition inside a Concession, which is then used as Evidence for a broader Justification. This NLP method parses the text into an RST tree and calculates its maximum and average dependency depth. A text structured as a long, flat list of sequential claims lacks the deep cognitive architecture of human reasoning and is highly indicative of machine generation.
useCase: Analyzing long-form arguments, argumentative essays, and persuasive writing where the logical structure feels suspiciously like a simple, bulleted list disguised as prose.
strengths:
• Highly effective at exposing the fundamental architectural weakness of autoregressive LLMs (lack of top-down planning).
• Extremely difficult for a prompt engineer to bypass, as humans cannot easily instruct an AI to mathematically increase its RST tree depth.
• Operates at the macro-document level, making it completely immune to word-level synonym swapping.
limitations:
• Computationally expensive; parsing deep RST trees on large documents requires significant processing power.
• May yield false positives on naturally 'flat' human writing, such as instruction manuals, chronological narratives, or lists.
• Less effective on very short texts (under 200 words) where deep hierarchical structures cannot naturally form.
parameters:
Analysis: Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST) Parsing & Sentence-Level Segmentation
Metric: Maximum and Average Discourse Tree Depth (Topological Distance from Root)
Output: 0-100 Discourse Shallowness (Architectural Flatness) Score
accuracy: High — 75-85% on argumentative and analytical texts. One of the most robust structural markers of synthetic text generation, targeting the core limitation of next-token prediction architectures.

references.title: Mann, W.C. & Thompson, S.A. (1988). Rhetorical Structure Theory. Text.
Ji, Y. & Eisenstein, J. (2014). Representation Learning for Text-level Discourse Parsing. ACL.
